unverified: The sequence of the example case (Monday 7:40, Sunday night, Friday 6:05 p.m., Jess's email) is invented and marked as an example.

That option A (second drive plugged in) and B (always-syncing cloud folder) don't protect you is Scutoria's interpretation of S1 (connected drives and connected cloud storage were encrypted too); marked as interpretation on screen.
The 3-2-1 rule and regular testing (S1) are not used in this version, to keep it to one step.

hook_candidates.spoken: What's left if your backup gets encrypted too?
You have a backup, so you're safe? Not if it's plugged in.
The NCSC has seen ransomware encrypt backup drives as well.
Your backup drive stays plugged in? Then ransomware can encrypt it too.
Monday, 7:40 a.m. No file will open, and neither will the backup.
hook_candidates.on_screen: MON 07:40 · The backup is gone too
hook_candidates.visual: clock, the colleague's email arrives as a paper card, the backup line is marked

beats.spoken: Monday, 7:40 a.m. Jess from the office writes: No file will open. And the backup drive plugged into the computer is encrypted too.

mail.subject: Nothing will open
lines: The backup drive on the PC too:

beats.spoken: And everything was set up. A backup every evening, automatically. Target: a USB drive. It's always plugged in, which is handy. But according to the NCSC, ransomware can spread to attached drives automatically.

fact.text: Malware can spread to attached drives automatically.

beats.spoken: Let's rewind. Sunday night, ransomware starts and encrypts everything, the drive included. Friday, 6:05 p.m.: the backup finishes, and the drive stays plugged in. That's the moment one small move was missing.
What do you change? A: Add a second drive, also plugged in. B: Add a cloud folder that syncs all the time. C: Unplug the drive after every backup. Remember your choice.

options.text: Unplug the drive after each backup

beats.spoken: The right answer is C. The NCSC's rule: at any given time, at least one backup is offline. When a drive isn't in use, disconnect it. A and B stay connected. The NCSC has even seen connected cloud storage encrypted.

card.title: One copy always offline
card.sub: unplug the drive after every backup

beats.spoken: A backup only protects you if one copy is offline. So: unplug the drive after every backup. What would you have picked? Tell me in the comments.
